title: RBA lacks consistency on interest rates
content:
# RBA lacks consistency on interest rates

Sunday 25 October 2026

The Reserve Bank of Australia's recent messaging on inflation and rates has been mixed, and interest rate expectations have swung widely as a result.

At last month's meeting the Board took a clearly hawkish line: it voted unanimously to raise the cash rate by 25 basis points to 4.60%, named inflation as its top priority, and said it was prepared to lift rates again if required.

The Minutes that followed carried the same tone, dwelling on upside risks to inflation, capacity pressure in the domestic economy, and the chance that a higher neutral rate leaves policy less restrictive than it looks.

The remainder of the article is behind a subscriber paywall.
rationale: The 25 Oct digest intro opened 'The RBA raised the cash rate to 4.60%' — a September decision this article restates as background. The content is a paraphrase of the free preview ingestion stored, not the original text (the repository is public); it keeps the same structure: a new development (inconsistent messaging) followed by the restated rate decision.
